dogecoin.text: C'mon people. Now I see Guy Fieri is being blamed for this latest Dogecoin charge? Some of these markets are like those deep cut ads urging you to click to see what happen to stars of TV shows you watched 20 years ago...

Dogecoin ($DOGEUSD) has seen its volatility stepped up sharply today. As high as 0.60 and significantly outpacing Ethereum and Bitcoin. Don't think that is a relative fundamental appeal considerable, rather looks to be preference for momentum (speculative appetite) https://t.co/CPt74iw9Rp
Dogecoin was less than 0.05 three months ago. Its high fell just shy of 0.70 today. Currently at 0.598. It isn't deep value. It is appetite for volatility and celebrity endorsement

Cryptos trade over the weekend unlike most other exchange-based markets. That along with Elon Musk's frequent social media references to Bitcoin and Dogecoin these past months have made his Saturday Night Live appearance an unusual 'market event'

There is some very interesting event risk over the opening half of this coming week of trade. It starts with Elon Musk hosting SNL tonight for Dogecoin traders and moves into US inflation data to as means to stir the ongoing Fed debate and Dollar https://t.co/Y16VeBGuY1 https://t.co/LXhjv7ToWC
So, is Ethereum considered a 'value' market to new Dogecoin traders?

There is a 'buy the dip' quality to the rebound in risk assets following yesterday's volatility. The Nasdaq 100 to Dow ratio shows preference for the outperforming tech sector of the past five years and Dogecoin soundly outpacing Bitcoin https://t.co/pRqSKcbMhx

If you were to make a basket of assets that was 'peak speculative appetite', what would you include in it? In 2021, my basket would have included meme stocks, Dogecoin, SPACs, ARK ETFs among other things. What now?
What comes at the crossroads of Tesla, SpaceX, Dogecoin and Twitter?
